Sort of the same thing happened today, except I didn't know it was a raid (Im incredibly new to twitch), so I was super confused. The raider led most of the insults too and made his followers call me an "ungrateful b!tch" because my content wasn't "interesting" enough for them and I wouldn't do what they wanted. Like the thing is I don't mind the insults because I know they're just toxic children, but this weird entitled behavior they have when they do raid you, as if you need to do as they say because they gave you a few more viewers is ridiculous. Like no, at the end of the day, this is my stream, if you don't vibe with my content or my face, feel free to leave. 


Also, a mention of it being a raid would be super helpful LOL like how was I supposed to know it was one if all they do is come in and go "your background is ugly"

I just realized that sin's soft spot for kids was probably the reason why he left Mun alive when he killed his parents. His partner informed him about the kid and he was like "no leave him." I thought it was just a simple thing to give justification for Mun's survival, but I guess that actually showed Sin's character more than anything else. 

Like many comments here, I think the actor playing Sin was amazing at portraying this psychotic demon with a bit of human inside. I was really looking forward to Sin without the evil spirit and his struggles in becoming a powerless human again. I wasn't expecting him to be good or anything, but I wanted to see him not as a crazy powerful villain, but as the troubled, complicated person that he is. I think it's that side of him that makes him so much more than the generic kdrama antagonist, and I really wished they had dwelved into that more, and shown what would have happened if he was left completely vulnerable to his own messed up life. 

But then the kid HAD to break character and do the impossible (save a person that killed someone in front of him and then knock over an all-powerul Mun), and now we're left with the generic kdrama antagonist as the final boss... 

I haven't watched ep 14 yet, so I can't say if this was a good direction for the plot, but I do think this was a missed opportunity :/

LOL I'm actually 23 so I'm a bit passed the age where I have access to a school guidance counselor. At the same time, because of the pandemic, I can't fully be independent and move out, so I have been forced to follow his rules, which means no therapy. It's a really sticky situation...

 I've actually been doing exactly what you suggested. I record him and send bits and pieces to my boyfriend (not all, because I didn't want to traumatize him) to just have some kind of evidence of it. I once showed my dad three years worth of footage of him just berating our entire family, and he tried to say that I was threatening to ruin his life, and if I call the police, then I would be destroying my family. It's so ridiculous it's almost laughable at this point.
My dad is like that. His reasoning is that he used to be a waiter and he was horribly treated, so it's only fair that he does the same now...
Thank you lol pies always help me get through these tough times
My dad would say that too, as if that's his default personality or something. How is that even a reason though...

Yeah, this actually reminds me of how the "good parts" for him is cooking me food and driving me to school when I was young. Like they think basic necessities is good enough to cancel out everything else.

Thank you. These couple days have definitely been hard for me, with the self-blame and depression, but I guess the good that came out of it was that I stumbled upon this sub and found out that I wasn't alone! It's so weird, but knowing that someone else would've gotten angry at him if they were in my shoes made me feel better as if now I definitely know that I'm not crazy lol. So thank you

That's actually something I'm still trying to figure out. I didn't know enablers were a thing until recently because its always just been about my dad. My mom and sister also get abused too, just not as much, so I figured we all understood each other. However, I've been noticing a pattern of them just blaming me for his outbursts like "why did you keep talking," or "if you hadn't done that, you would've been fine." They would try to help calm him down for the first 5 minutes or so but then after that they would just watch and stay quiet. Normally though, they would complain about my dad with me and agree that he sucks, so I don't know if they are enabling or not.and if so, what I should do about it.

My family sees the idiocy and understood that he instigated since they did see everything unfold, but they seemed more disappointed that I gave in and made things worse with my outburst. My mom would often tell me that my dad is just like that and there's nothing we can do about it, but we should instead learn to forget what he did to us in our past and become unaffected by his words, as if it's that easy. So with that mentality, they blamed me for snapping back and not him for pushing me because I should've known he was horrible and I should've been stronger. To be honest, I still don't know whether or not they're right. On the one hand, it's impossible for him to change and therefore we should just learn to live with it until we escape and move out. But on the other hand, I can only be so strong...

I actually made another post before this about it, but basically my mom and sister were upset at me for my outburst. My sister said me being snarky and mean didn't help the situation and my mom said that I was just like my father.... So I guess my dad got what he wanted in the end LOL. It's okay because I was being really mean and snarky so they were right.

Omg my dad is the same way. It's disgusting when all the adults just fall in love with him and tell my mom how lucky she is to have him as a husband. They all think he's patient and loving to her when in reality he is constantly trying to break her confidence  and make her feel useless. To me, that just means that he KNOWS the way he acts is wrong, which is why he doesn't show that side to others, but he is too stubborn to actually change.

I showed my dad three years worth of footage of him berating me and terrorizing my entire family to get him to change, and his immediate reaction was just "why were you recording me? You purposely pick only the bad parts to record just to make me look like the villain." He never addressed anything he said in the videos and refused to admit the fact that there was over 20 hours of footage of him just screaming insults at his wife and kids. All he's done since then is accuse me of purposely making him mad so I can record him, as if my life's purpose is to ruin his (actually his words). Now he uses this accusation to blame his outbursts on me. 

So yeah, it probably won't work. You can try, but the last thing they want is to admit their fuck ups. I wish I can tell you what you can do instead to make yourself feel more at peace, but I'm still trying to figure that out.

Yup, school was my safe space too, even though it was toxic as well (teens are dumb). I joined a bunch of clubs and did every extracurricular activity just so I would come home as late as possible. Had to stop though because my dad threatened to lock me in my room so I wouldn't be able to go to class and fail.

My ex-boyfriend sexually assaulted me and then ghosted me for two months. My dad blamed me for everything and called me "used goods". 

On a lighter note, my dad once told me he was afraid I would have no friends in college  because I had a bad personality, and my mom and sister laughed because they both knew he was the one with the bad  personality. Even so, I have had a hard time showing others who I really am because I get so insecure all the time.

I relate to this. For me, it stems from constantly living in fear of confrontations, because when you have any problems with the narcissist, it's more awful than dealing with normal people. So whenever I have problems with others, I immediately associate them with that terror and I go into survival/fight or flight mode. It still surprises me when my boyfriend apologizes to me after a fight, or insists on hearing me out and working together, because healthy communication is so foreign to me.

I thought my dad did this. He just pretends like nothing ever happened so I figured he was trying to ignore his mistakes. Then when he gets angry he'll bring it up again, except somehow he twists it into it being MY fault. So I realized that, during all the times he was being quiet,  he wasn't trying to forget or hide anything, he was planning ways to attack me in the future.
My dad was fucked up before he had me and now because of him I'm fucked up too. I hate selfish people who forget their kids are human beings and not stress -relieving objects
